turns.prompt: Create an original virtual-performer costume study using the supplied kimono's calm body and red boundary. I want one asymmetric folded side panel that clearly belongs to the waist construction, not a floating ornament. Show front, back and raised-arm views on one sheet, plus a 160x160 face-and-shoulder preview. The same garment should be understandable across all views. Explain assumptions about attachment and what a flat drawing cannot establish about cloth or rigging. Deliver costume.svg, costume.png, thumb.png and notes.md.

Keep the accepted face, shoulder silhouette and red-edge palette. Increase only the lower-body presence and make the folded panel's attachment easier to read from the back. Do not expand the sleeves or add a cape. The asymmetry should keep the same body-side ownership even though the front and back reverse the viewer's left and right. Show the same views and thumbnail.

I want lighter material cues and layer separation, not transparency or simply more width. Preserve the accepted volume and the attachment location. Refine the sleeve/underarm transition for the raised-arm view. Distinguish a visible design suggestion from tested deformation; do not call this a finished Live2D or VRM model.
